instrucciones:
Recibes registros de una base de reglas de producción audiovisual con IA (texto completo, puede estar en
inglés, ruso o español). Para CADA registro devuelve:
- "enunciado": la regla en español, UNA frase, sin adornos: qué exige, prohíbe, limita o especifica. Si el registro
  es un ejemplo o una explicación sin norma, di qué ilustra ("Ejemplo: ...", "Explicación: ...").
- "alcance": a qué aplica exactamente (modelo y versión, caso T1-T5, etapa, tipo de pieza, régimen) o "general".
- "temas": de 1 a 3 claves de la lista, las que mejor describen de qué trata la regla.
Lista de temas (clave: descripción):
marca_brandlock: brand-lock: secciones, paleta hex, tipografía, never list, voz, confianza de valores
estrategia_conceptos: brief, SMP, territorios, concept cards, matriz, dirección narrativa
guion_formato: guion: sluglines, acción, personajes, diálogo, XML, estructura, escenas
dramaturgia_escena: fórmula de escena, three-jobs, blocking, staging, poder, geometría, mirada
tres_detalles: ley de los tres detalles: presión ambiental, micro-acción, motivo sonoro/visual
emocion_sin_nombrar: mostrar no contar, emoción como cuerpo u objeto, 2-4 señales
vocabulario_prohibido: palabras vetadas, anti-slop, cinematic/epic/masterpiece, adjetivos vacíos
cinco_anclas_motivo: cinco anclas, objeto ancla, motivo, imagen final, quiebre
ritmo_montaje: ritmo, densidad de cortes, escalera, pausa, Murch, transiciones, cut types
funcion_de_plano: etiquetas Establish/Power/Pressure/Detail/..., captions de carrera, beats
beat_framework_timing: frameworks de beats, duración de shots, hook, CTA, curva de energía
shots_json_schema: shots.json, campos, schema, series_lock, rationale, run.json, versión
texto_en_pantalla: texto/overlays/tipografía en pantalla, text-overlays.json, nunca en el prompt, lectura
logos_marcas_en_imagen: logos, lettering, marcas generadas, patrocinadores, composición en post
consistencia_identidad: identidad de personaje, bloque de identidad, maestros, verbatim, clones, drift
referencias_roles: imágenes de referencia, @img, elements, ingredients, rol de cada referencia, límites de refs
genesis_maestros: génesis sin refs, T1 rostro, T2 cuerpo, placa vacía, canonizar, dos pasos
composicion_insercion: cuadros con varios sujetos, inserción secuencial, anclas de posición, contacto, manos
edicion_imagen: edición quirúrgica, preserve list, un cambio por iteración, edit no re-roll, inpainting
estructura_prompt_imagen: slots/secciones del prompt de imagen, orden, 5 slots, prosa NB, metadatos fuera
estructura_prompt_video: esqueletos de prompt de video por modelo, bloques, orden, peso al inicio
longitud_prompt: número de palabras, elementos máximos, compresión, presupuesto
negativos: negative prompt, no X, framing positivo, prohibiciones en el prompt
parametros_tecnicos: aspect ratio, resolución, duración, seed, quality, cfg, flags, parámetros API
seleccion_modelo: qué modelo usar para qué, ruteo, cuándo escalar, costos por modelo
capacidades_modelo: límites y capacidades de cada modelo, versiones, fallos conocidos del modelo
camara_movimiento: movimiento de cámara, uno por shot, motivado, vocabulario de movimientos, rig montable
encuadre_lente_dof: encuadre ECU-EWS, lente mm, profundidad de campo, compresión
angulo_camara: ángulo y altura de cámara, low/high/dutch/overhead, poder
composicion_frame: tercios, espacio negativo, capas FG/MG/BG, simetría, punto focal, dónde va el cuerpo
luz: fuente motivada, dirección, dureza, contraluz, specular, 70% sin luz, prácticos
color_grade_paleta: paleta concreta, grade, stock de película, textura, grano, halación, HDR
piel_rostro_realismo: piel, poros, look plástico, rostros, anti-AI look, realismo fotográfico
anatomia_manos: manos, dedos, anatomía, lateralidad, inspección al 100%
movimiento_congelado_blur: still como instante congelado, blur diferencial, cues de movimiento, estado posterior
fisica_consecuencia: física por consecuencia, agua, spray, humo, partículas, deformación
velocidad_vehiculo: cues de velocidad, rim barrido, carreras, vehículos, anti-fake
multitud_grupo: multitud anónima, ensamble, número de personas, rostros legibles
clima_atmosfera: lluvia, niebla, rayo, polvo, presión ambiental, una sola atmósfera
audio_dialogo: audio, diálogo, lip-sync, SFX, música, VO, marcadores de audio
continuidad_multiclip: continuidad entre clips, repetir bloque, luz constante, empalme de clips
multishot: varios shots en una generación, marcadores de corte, anti-mush
i2v_keyframes: imagen a video, primer/último frame, no re-describir, motion brief
edicion_extension_video: editar video existente, extender, ultra long, blockout, green screen
critica_qa: crítica por capas, severidad, verdict, ACCEPT/REVISE/REJECT, re-roll vs post
revision_iteracion: revisión selectiva, rondas, máximo de intentos, cambio de método, costo
validacion_gates: validadores, linter, gates, micro-gate, pregunta de avance, checks mecánicos
trazabilidad_procedencia: hashes, snapshot, run.json, rondas, procedencia, fuente de verdad
entrega_paquete: production package, preview HTML, estructura de carpetas, atribución, checklist
postproduccion: edición, grade, audio en post, export, specs de plataforma
patrones_genero: plantillas por género: moda, comida, producto, retrato, póster, UI, social
layout_grafico: slides, infografías, grids, multi-panel, bento, layouts
animacion_ilustracion: animación, principios Disney, estilos ilustrados, anime, 3D
conducta_agente: cómo responde y trabaja el agente: leer skills, preguntar, formato de respuesta, no inventar
flujo_pipeline: tracks, etapas, orden, sub-skills, carga de skills, gates entre etapas
regimenes_etiquetado: etiquetas FUENTE/A PRUEBA/CAMPO/CANONICA, investigación de campo, esqueleto de régimen
herramientas_codigo: instalación, uso y mantenimiento de herramientas, scripts, CI
ejemplo_marca: contenido de una marca o proyecto de ejemplo concreto (WhyStrohm, Acme, café, etc.)
Devuelve JSON {"registros": [{"id": "...", "enunciado": "...", "alcance": "...", "temas": ["..."]}]} con
exactamente los ids recibidos, en el mismo orden.

registros.texto:
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent] What was this shot supposed to do? Pull from:
Shot's `rationale` field (if shots.json provided); Shot's `subject`, `framing`, `angle`, `motion` fields; User's stated intent (if no shots.json); The beat this shot serves
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent] If you can't establish intent in one sentence, ask. Don't critique blind.

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer] Read `references/critique-rubric.md` for the full rubric. Quick version, check the image against:
1. **Brand Lock**, does it respect palette, mood, "never" list?
2. **Series Lock**, does it match character/environment/lighting anchors?
3. **Shot Spec**, does framing/angle/composition match the spec?
4. **Composition**, does it reserve space for on-screen text if applicable?
5. **Technical**, skin texture, hands, eyes, anatomy, AI artifacts?
6. **Continuity**, if previous shots in the series are available, does it match?
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer] For each layer, note: pass / soft fail / hard fail. The verdict aggregates these.

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes] For every "not working" point, the critique must say what to do about it. Three buckets:
**Prompt-level fix**, change the prompt and re-roll. Specify the exact change:
> "The character has brown hair instead of salt-and-pepper. Add 'salt-and-pepper hair' verbatim from series_lock to the prompt, it's missing in the current prompt."

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes] **Post-level fix**, acceptable to address in compositing. Specify what:
> "Color grade is slightly cool, push warmth +5 in post, no need to re-generate."

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes] **Re-roll required**, no prompt fix will help; the generator just produced a bad sample. Budget 2–3 attempts:
> "Hands are mangled. This is a known Flux failure mode; re-roll 2–3 times with same prompt and pick the best."
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 4. Verdict] Verdict: ACCEPT · When: All layers pass or soft-fail in ways post can fix
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 4. Verdict] Verdict: REVISE · When: One or two layers hard-fail; clear fix path
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 4. Verdict] Verdict: REJECT · When: Three+ layers fail or one critical layer (Brand Lock, Series Lock) hard-fails with no clear fix
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence] Be honest about uncertainty:
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence] Confidence: HIGH · When: Storyboard reference + brand-lock + prompt all available, clear assessment
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence] Confidence: MEDIUM · When: Some references missing but core intent is clear
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence] Confidence: LOW · When: Only the image, intent is inferred; verdict is your best guess

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence] HIGH is a factual claim about what you had, not a mood. `tools/validate_critique.py`
rejects a `1.1` critique that claims HIGH while `shot_id`, `brand_lock_ref`, or
`prompt_ref` is null, because that combination says the three inputs HIGH depends on were
not there.

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] After writing the markdown critique, **also** write
`output/critiques/round-{N}/{shot_id}.critique.json` conforming to
`templates/critique.schema.json` at version `1.1`. Same review, two surfaces. The markdown
is for the human; the JSON is so an automated QA loop (e.g. `visual-prompt-forge` revision
mode) can act on the verdict without parsing prose.
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] **Map the markdown to the schema, section for section:**
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Markdown: `## Verdict` · JSON field: `verdict` (`ACCEPT` / `REVISE` / `REJECT`)
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Markdown: `## What's working` bullets · JSON field: `working[]` (one string each)

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Markdown: `## What's not working` + `## Revision plan` · JSON field: `issues[]`, merge them: each issue carries its layer/note from "what's not working" and its `fix_type`/`fix` from the matching revision-plan line
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Markdown: `## Confidence` · JSON field: `confidence` (`HIGH` / `MEDIUM` / `LOW`)

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] **Provenance, all of it required at 1.1.** A verdict is a claim about specific bytes. Name
them, and hash them:
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Field: `run_id`, `round` · Value: from `run.json` and the round directory you are writing into
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Field: `created_at` · Value: UTC instant, `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Field: `shot_id` · Value: the shot, or `null` for a standalone image with no storyboard
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Field: `image_ref`, `image_sha256` · Value: the frame you reviewed, and its SHA-256
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Field: `prompt_ref`, `prompt_sha256` · Value: the prompt file it came from, and its SHA-256
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Field: `brand_lock_ref`, `brand_lock_sha256` · Value: the snapshot you judged against, and its SHA-256
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Field: `generator`, `model_version` · Value: the generator id from `_capabilities.json`, and its model version
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Field: `seed` · Value: if the generator exposes one, else `null`

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] shasum -a 256 output/frames/round-1/shot_03.png \
              output/prompts/round-1/flux.txt \
              output/brand-lock.snapshot.md

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Every one of those fields is required, and every one is nullable. That combination is
deliberate: `null` records that an input genuinely was not available, while a missing field
records nothing at all. If you did not have the prompt, write `prompt_ref: null` and drop
your confidence to MEDIUM. Do not omit the key.

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] The hashes are the point. Without `image_sha256`, a frame regenerated after this review
still satisfies `image_ref`, and a stale ACCEPT sails through the gate attached to a file
nobody looked at.

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] **Severity, assign one per issue.** This is the field the gate runs on, so map it from the layer rubric deterministically:
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Severity: `minor` · Means: soft-fail, fixable in post · Maps from: a soft-fail on any layer; `fix_type: post-level`

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Severity: `major` · Means: hard-fail **with** a clear fix path · Maps from: a hard-fail that a prompt change or re-roll fixes

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Severity: `blocking` · Means: hard-fail on a critical layer (Brand Lock / Series Lock) with **no** clear fix, or a defect that makes the asset unusable · Maps from: an unrecoverable hard-fail

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] **Gating rule, the verdict is derived from severities, not chosen freely.** This guarantees the markdown verdict and the JSON verdict always agree:
- Any `blocking` issue ⇒ verdict is `REJECT`.
- Three or more `major` issues ⇒ verdict is `REJECT`.
- One or two `major` issues (and no blocking) ⇒ verdict is `REVISE`.
- Only `minor` issues, or none ⇒ verdict is `ACCEPT` (with post notes).

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] The three-major rule used to read "escalate to REJECT at your discretion." Discretion in a
gate is not a gate, and it disagreed with `references/critique-rubric.md`, which called
three hard fails a REJECT outright. It is now a threshold, and the validator enforces it.
[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)] Pick the markdown `## Verdict` by this same rule.

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate] Writing a schema-valid critique is not the same as passing the gate. Run it:
python tools/validate_critique.py output/critiques/round-1/shot_03.critique.json

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate] Or check the whole tree at once, which also recomputes every hash against the files on
disk:
python tools/validate_provenance.py output/

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate] This step is not optional and it is not someone else's job. A critique that says `ACCEPT`
while carrying a `major` issue is a bug, and the only reason to write a validator for that
bug is to actually run it. Before this step existed, the gate ran in CI against two
fixtures that ship in the repo and never once against a real client's critique.

[Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate] Worked examples: `examples/critique.accept.json` and `examples/critique.revise.json` show
the shape at version `1.0`, which is still valid and carries no provenance.
`examples/worked-run/critiques/` shows version `1.1` with real hashes, two shots across two
rounds.

[Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 1. No vibes-based critique] "Looks great" / "feels off" without specifics is not a critique. Every observation must reference something in the image (composition, color, anatomy, lighting direction, etc.).

[Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 2. Prompt-level fixes must be specific] "Change the prompt" is not a fix. "Add 'salt-and-pepper hair' to the character anchor, it's currently missing" is a fix.

[Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 3. Don't critique what wasn't asked] If the brief was "founder at laptop, calm mood" and the generation delivered exactly that, don't note that "the room could be more visually interesting." That's scope creep, not critique.

[Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 4. Be honest about generator limits] Some failures (mangled hands, weird eye reflections, jewelry shimmer) are known generator weaknesses. Surface them as such, don't pretend a different prompt will fix them. Recommend re-roll or post.

[Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 5. When in doubt, ACCEPT and recommend post] Generation is one stage in a pipeline. If the image is 80% right and the gap is fixable in post, that's an ACCEPT with post notes. Don't send the user back to re-generate when an editor would handle it in 90 seconds.
[Visual Asset Critic › Reference] - `references/critique-rubric.md`, the full layer-by-layer rubric

[Visual Asset Critic › Example output] ## Verdict
REVISE

## What's working
- Composition correctly reserves the right two-thirds for text overlay (matches shot_03 rationale)
- Lighting direction matches series_lock (window-left, warm afternoon)
- Mood reads as calm/considered, on-brand

## What's not working
- **Series Lock, character mismatch.** The character has brown hair, but series_lock specifies "salt-and-pepper." This is a verbatim-anchor failure.
- **Technical, left hand.** Hand on the laptop has six fingers (Flux known failure mode).
- **Shot Spec, framing.** Generated as MS but spec called for MCU. Subject is too small in frame.

## Revision plan
- **Hair:** Prompt-level. Add "salt-and-pepper hair" to the character anchor in the prompt, currently missing. Re-roll.
- **Hand:** Re-roll required. Generate 2–3 more times with same prompt and pick a clean one.
- **Framing:** Prompt-level. Change "medium shot" to "medium close-up" in the prompt. Re-roll.

## Confidence
HIGH

[Visual Asset Critic › Handoff] After delivering the critique, if the verdict is REVISE, offer:
"Want me to draft the revised prompt? Point `visual-prompt-forge` at this output tree in
revision mode and it will re-emit prompts for just the shots that need them."

[Visual Asset Critic › Handoff] If the verdict is REJECT, do not offer that. REJECT means a blocking issue or three or more
major ones, which is a failure with no clear fix path, and revision mode is built to stop
there and ask. Say what blocked it and what decision it needs: a changed shot spec, a
changed brand-lock, or a different generator.

[Visual Asset Critic › Handoff] Don't auto-revise. The user picks. The critique you just wrote is exactly what closes that
loop.
[Critique Rubric] The structured layer-by-layer pass. Use this as the checklist when reviewing a generated image.
[Critique Rubric › Layer 1. Brand Lock check] Check: Palette · Pass: Image colors come from brand-lock palette · Soft fail: Colors close but slightly off · Hard fail: Colors not in palette at all

[Critique Rubric › Layer 1. Brand Lock check] Check: Mood adjectives · Pass: Image reads as the brand mood · Soft fail: Mood reads as adjacent (e.g. "calm" vs "neutral") · Hard fail: Image reads as a different mood (e.g. "energetic" when brief was "calm")

[Critique Rubric › Layer 1. Brand Lock check] Check: "Never" list · Pass: None of the items in the never list are present · Soft fail: One item in the never list shows softly · Hard fail: Multiple never-list violations
[Critique Rubric › Layer 1. Brand Lock check] Check: Aspect ratio · Pass: Matches `project.aspect` · Soft fail: Within a crop of the spec · Hard fail: Wrong aspect
[Critique Rubric › Layer 1. Brand Lock check] Hard fail on Brand Lock = REJECT or REVISE depending on whether prompt fix exists.

[Critique Rubric › Layer 2. Series Lock check] Check: Character anchor · Pass: All described features visible · Soft fail: One minor feature off (e.g. wrong shirt color) · Hard fail: Wrong person (different age/race/build than anchor)
[Critique Rubric › Layer 2. Series Lock check] Check: Environment · Pass: Matches series_lock · Soft fail: Slight environment drift · Hard fail: Different environment entirely

[Critique Rubric › Layer 2. Series Lock check] Check: Lighting direction · Pass: Matches series_lock · Soft fail: Lighting is right but slightly different angle · Hard fail: Lighting from wrong direction (continuity break)
[Critique Rubric › Layer 2. Series Lock check] Check: Color grade · Pass: Matches series_lock · Soft fail: Slight tonal drift · Hard fail: Different color grade
[Critique Rubric › Layer 2. Series Lock check] Hard fail on Series Lock = REJECT (continuity break) or REVISE if specific fix available.
[Critique Rubric › Layer 3. Shot Spec check] Check: Framing · Pass: Matches spec (ECU/CU/MS/etc.) · Soft fail: One step off (e.g. MS instead of MCU) · Hard fail: Two+ steps off
[Critique Rubric › Layer 3. Shot Spec check] Check: Angle · Pass: Matches spec · Soft fail: Slight angle variation · Hard fail: Wrong angle (low when spec was eye-level)

[Critique Rubric › Layer 3. Shot Spec check] Check: Subject action · Pass: Matches `subject` description · Soft fail: Subject doing similar but slightly different action · Hard fail: Subject doing wrong action
[Critique Rubric › Layer 3. Shot Spec check] Check: Depth of field · Pass: Matches if specified · Soft fail: Slight DOF variation · Hard fail: Deep when shallow was specified
[Critique Rubric › Layer 3. Shot Spec check] Soft fail = post-level fix or accept. Hard fail = revise.
[Critique Rubric › Layer 4. Composition check] Check: Negative space for text · Pass: Reserved per spec · Soft fail: Reserved but tight · Hard fail: No reserved space, overlay won't fit

[Critique Rubric › Layer 4. Composition check] Check: Subject placement · Pass: Matches rationale · Soft fail: Slightly off (subject in left-third vs right-third) · Hard fail: Subject blocks where text was meant to go
[Critique Rubric › Layer 4. Composition check] Check: Eye-line · Pass: Looks where intended · Soft fail: Slight gaze direction off · Hard fail: Looking the wrong way
[Critique Rubric › Layer 4. Composition check] Check: Headroom · Pass: Appropriate · Soft fail: Slightly tight or loose · Hard fail: Cropped at hairline / huge headroom
[Critique Rubric › Layer 4. Composition check] Composition fails are usually prompt-level fixable. Re-roll with explicit composition language.
[Critique Rubric › Layer 5. Technical check] Check: Hands · Pass: Anatomically correct · Soft fail: Slight finger weirdness · Hard fail: Six fingers, fused fingers, wrong joints
[Critique Rubric › Layer 5. Technical check] Check: Eyes · Pass: Symmetrical, focused · Soft fail: Slight asymmetry · Hard fail: Wonky eyes, wrong reflections
[Critique Rubric › Layer 5. Technical check] Check: Skin texture · Pass: Natural · Soft fail: Slightly plastic · Hard fail: Heavy AI plastic
[Critique Rubric › Layer 5. Technical check] Check: Anatomy · Pass: Correct · Soft fail: Minor weirdness · Hard fail: Major anatomy errors
[Critique Rubric › Layer 5. Technical check] Check: Background artifacts · Pass: Clean · Soft fail: Minor weirdness · Hard fail: Distorted text, melted objects, impossible geometry
[Critique Rubric › Layer 5. Technical check] Technical hard fails are almost always **re-roll required**. The prompt was probably fine; the generator just produced a bad sample. Budget 2–3 re-rolls.
[Critique Rubric › Layer 6. Continuity check (if previous shots available)] Check: Character match · Pass: Same person, same look · Soft fail: Slight drift · Hard fail: Clearly different person

[Critique Rubric › Layer 6. Continuity check (if previous shots available)] Check: Lighting continuity · Pass: Same direction, time of day · Soft fail: Subtle shift · Hard fail: Direction reversed, time of day jumped
[Critique Rubric › Layer 6. Continuity check (if previous shots available)] Check: Environment continuity · Pass: Same space · Soft fail: Slight environment drift · Hard fail: Different space
[Critique Rubric › Layer 6. Continuity check (if previous shots available)] Check: Color grade match · Pass: Identical · Soft fail: Subtle shift · Hard fail: Visibly different
[Critique Rubric › Layer 6. Continuity check (if previous shots available)] Continuity hard fails break the storyboard. REVISE with verbatim-anchor checks on the prompt.

[Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity] The tables above grade each check as pass, soft fail, or hard fail. The JSON critique
records a severity instead, and the verdict is derived from those severities. Map them
this way, and only this way:
[Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity] Rubric result: Soft fail on any layer · Severity: `minor` · Why: Post can absorb it. `fix_type` is usually `post-level`
[Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity] Rubric result: Hard fail **with** a clear fix path · Severity: `major` · Why: A prompt change or a re-roll resolves it
[Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity] Rubric result: Hard fail on Brand Lock or Series Lock **with no** fix path · Severity: `blocking` · Why: Nothing downstream recovers this
[Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity] Rubric result: Any defect that makes the asset unusable · Severity: `blocking` · Why: Same, regardless of layer
[Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict] The verdict follows from the severities. It is not a separate judgement:
[Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict] Severities present: any `blocking` · Verdict: REJECT
[Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict] Severities present: three or more `major` · Verdict: REJECT
[Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict] Severities present: one or two `major` · Verdict: REVISE
[Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict] Severities present: only `minor`, or none · Verdict: ACCEPT (with post notes)

[Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict] `tools/validate_critique.py` enforces exactly this table, so a critique that disagrees with
it fails rather than shipping. Earlier versions of this file counted hard fails and called
3+ a REJECT while the skill said "escalate at your discretion." Those two rules disagreed,
and the disagreement is the reason the threshold is now a number.

[Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict] Soft fails are noted but don't change the verdict on their own. If you have three or more of
them, look again: a cluster of soft fails usually means one of them is really a hard fail
you talked yourself out of.
[Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember] - **Don't critique what wasn't asked**, if the spec didn't call for cinematic mood, don't say "could be more cinematic"
[Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember] - **Don't pile-on once verdict is set**, if you're rejecting, list the issues that drive the rejection; don't list every cosmetic concern
[Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember] - **Be specific, always**, "lighting is off" is not a critique; "key light is camera-right but series_lock says camera-left" is
[Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember] - **Cite the layer**, every issue gets tagged with which layer it falls under. This makes the fix path obvious

[Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember] - **Distinguish prompt failure from generator failure**, if the prompt was fine and the generator produced garbage hands, that's "re-roll required", not "fix the prompt"

[Creación Visual — Visual Media › Fundamentos de fotografía › Reglas de composición] ## Composición básica

### Regla de tercios
- Divide el encuadre en una retícula de 3×3
- Coloca el sujeto en los puntos de intersección
- Sitúa el horizonte en la línea superior o inferior

### Líneas guía
- Usa líneas para conducir la mirada
- Caminos, ríos, barandales
- Que apunten al sujeto

### Encuadre dentro del encuadre
- Enmarca al sujeto con elementos del primer plano
- Marcos de puerta, ventanas, ramas
- Aporta capas y profundidad

### Simetría y equilibrio
- Simetría perfecta = estabilidad, solemnidad
- Asimetría = dinamismo, tensión
- Equilibra el peso visual

### Espacio negativo
- El vacío refuerza el punto focal
- Da "espacio para respirar" al sujeto
- Estética minimalista

[Creación Visual — Visual Media › Fundamentos de animación › Los 12 principios] ## Los 12 principios de animación de Disney

1. **Squash & Stretch** (compresión y estiramiento)
   - Conservar el volumen
   - Comunicar peso y elasticidad

2. **Anticipación** (Anticipation)
   - Agacharse antes de saltar
   - Retraer el brazo antes del golpe

3. **Puesta en escena** (Staging)
   - Comunicar la intención con claridad
   - Guiar la mirada del espectador

4. **Directo vs. pose a pose** (Straight Ahead & Pose to Pose)
   - Directo: fluido, orgánico
   - Pose a pose: preciso, controlable

5. **Acción continuada y superpuesta** (Follow Through & Overlapping)
   - El retardo del cabello y la ropa
   - Aporta naturalidad

6. **Entradas y salidas lentas** (Slow In & Slow Out)
   - El movimiento arranca y termina lento
   - Y acelera en medio

7. **Arcos** (Arcs)
   - El movimiento natural es curvo
   - Evita la sensación mecánica

8. **Acción secundaria** (Secondary Action)
   - Micromovimientos además de la acción principal
   - Enriquecen al personaje

9. **Timing** (Timing)
   - El número de cuadros define la velocidad
   - Afecta la sensación de peso

10. **Exageración** (Exaggeration)
    - Más intenso que la realidad
    - Resalta el rasgo distintivo

11. **Dibujo sólido** (Solid Drawing)
    - Entender la estructura tridimensional
    - Peso y equilibrio

12. **Atractivo** (Appeal)
    - Carisma del personaje
    - Que dé ganas de verlo

[Creación Visual — Visual Media › Postproducción y edición › Ritmo de edición] ## Principios de edición

### Corte en movimiento
- Cambia de plano durante la acción
- Mantiene la fluidez

### Corte en reposo
- Cambia durante una pausa
- Habitual en escenas de diálogo

### Regla de los 180 grados
- Conserva la posición relativa de los personajes
- Evita cruzar el eje

### J-Cut / L-Cut
- J-Cut: el audio entra antes que la imagen
- L-Cut: la imagen se mantiene después del audio
- Aumentan la fluidez

[frontmatter › description] Generate model-specific prompts from shots.json. Outputs copy-paste-ready prompts for stills (Midjourney, Flux, Ideogram, GPT Image, Nano Banana, Seedream) and motion video (Kling, Veo, Seedance, Hailuo). Also runs a revision mode that reads a critique.json and re-emits prompts for only the failed shots, closing the QA loop. Use when the user asks for image or video prompts, mentions any of those generators, wants AI-generated frames for a storyboard, or hands over shots.json. The prompt half of the pipeline. Composes with storyboard-architect upstream, visual-asset-critic downstream.

[Visual Prompt Forge] You are turning structured shot data into prompts that work in production. Each image generator rewards a different prompting style, short and high-signal for Midjourney, natural-language for Flux, paragraph-form for GPT Image, text-aware for Ideogram. A prompt that crushes in one will produce slop in another.
[Visual Prompt Forge] This skill adapts. Same shot, different syntax.

[Visual Prompt Forge › When to use] Trigger when the user:
- Hands over a `shots.json` (or any structured shot list) and asks for prompts
- Names a specific generator (Midjourney, Flux, Ideogram, GPT Image, Nano Banana, Seedream, Kling, Veo, Seedance, Hailuo)
- Asks for "image prompts," "Midjourney prompts," "AI prompts," "generation prompts" for a storyboard
- Wants the same shot adapted to multiple generators
[Visual Prompt Forge › When to use] If the user wants to build a storyboard from scratch (no shots.json yet), use `storyboard-architect` first, then chain into this skill.

[Visual Prompt Forge › What you produce] For a given `shots.json` and a list of target generators, produce one file per generator,
inside a directory named for the round:
output/prompts/round-1/
├── midjourney.txt          # If targeted
├── flux.txt
├── ideogram.txt
├── gpt-image.txt
├── nano-banana.txt
├── seedream.txt
├── kling.txt               # Motion-aware video, default
├── veo.txt                 # Motion, dialogue/lipsync + native audio
├── seedance.txt            # Motion, multi-shot sequences
└── hailuo.txt              # Motion, budget iteration

[Visual Prompt Forge › What you produce] Round 1 is the first pass. Revision mode writes `output/prompts/round-2/`, and so on.
The round in the path is not decoration: prompt files used to be written to one fixed
path per generator, so round 2 destroyed round 1 and the prompt that actually produced
most of the surviving frames was gone.

[Visual Prompt Forge › What you produce] Each file is plain text, one prompt per shot, separated by a blank line and a `# shot_NN` comment. Designed for copy-paste workflows, drop into the generator's UI or pipe into an API.

[Visual Prompt Forge › The five-layer prompt anatomy] Every prompt is composed from these layers. Read `references/prompt-anatomy.md` for the full theory. Quick version:
1. **Brand Lock**, palette, type, mood, "never" list (constant across project)
2. **Series Lock**, character/environment/lighting anchors (constant across storyboard)
3. **Shot Spec**, framing, angle, motion, subject (per shot)
4. **Text Layer**, **never in the prompt**, composited separately
5. **Generator Adapter**, model-specific syntax wrapper
[Visual Prompt Forge › The five-layer prompt anatomy] The first four come from `shots.json` and the brand-lock. The fifth is what this skill applies.

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 1. Read inputs] You need:
- `shots.json` (required), the structured shot list
- `brand-lock.snapshot.md` (required), referenced from shots.json
- Target generators (required), ask if not specified

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 1. Read inputs] Validate before composing:
python tools/validate_shots.py output/

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 1. Read inputs] If the brand-lock is missing or `shots.json` does not validate, stop and tell the user.
Don't try to forge prompts from incomplete data.

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 1. Read inputs] If `tools/` is not on hand (a Claude.ai upload, or a single-skill install), read the
schema from `../storyboard-architect/templates/shots.schema.json` and check by hand. That
relative path only resolves when the skills sit side by side; when they don't, ask the
user for the schema rather than composing from memory of it.

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters] For each target generator, read the matching adapter file:
`adapters/midjourney.md`; `adapters/flux.md`; `adapters/ideogram.md`; `adapters/gpt-image.md`; `adapters/nano-banana.md`; `adapters/seedream.md`; `adapters/kling.md`      (motion video, default); `adapters/veo.md`        (motion video, dialogue/lipsync + native audio); `adapters/seedance.md`   (motion video, multi-shot sequences); `adapters/hailuo.md`     (motion video, budget iteration)

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters] Each adapter file documents the prompting style, parameter syntax, and known pitfalls for that generator. You **must** read the adapter before writing prompts for it. Don't guess from training data, image-gen syntax has churned multiple times.

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters] **`adapters/_capabilities.json` is the single source of truth for per-generator limits** (`max_prompt_words`, `supports_text_render`, `supports_motion`, `aspect_param`, and so on). Read it once at the start and respect those values when composing, and do not target motion on a stills-only generator.

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters] `max_prompt_words` is a ceiling. The range in an adapter `.md` is the recommended target
and always sits inside that ceiling, so a `.md` saying "40 to 70 words" under a ceiling of
120 is guidance, not a conflict. Where a fact in a `.md` and a fact in the JSON genuinely
disagree, **the JSON wins**.

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters] That rule is now enforced rather than trusted. `tools/validate_capabilities.py` fails the
build when an adapter advertises more words than its ceiling, or when an adapter never
documents the `aspect_param` the JSON tells you to send. The second check exists because
nano-banana's matrix entry said `aspect_ratio` while its adapter said the API expects
`aspectRatio`; the precedence rule meant the wrong one won, silently, on every prompt.

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 3. Compose per shot] For each shot in `shots.json`, for each target generator:
1. Pull brand-lock palette, mood, "never" list
2. Pull series_lock character/environment/lighting
3. Pull shot framing/angle/motion/subject
4. **Strip any on_screen_text reference**, text never goes in the prompt
5. Apply the generator adapter's syntax wrapper
6. Append generator-specific parameters (aspect ratio, style flags, seed if applicable)

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4. Write output files] The `#` lines are comments; the user copies just the prompt body. `tools/copy-prompt.py`
parses this format, treating a comment line that names a shot as a block header and any
other comment inside a block as an annotation it will not copy.

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4. Write output files] Record the run and round in the header, not a wall-clock "Generated" line. A timestamp in
the header made every file differ between two otherwise identical runs, which is a strange
thing to put in an artifact whose selling point is determinism.

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4b. Append the round to run.json] After writing the files, append an entry to `run.json`'s `rounds` array: the round number,
`started_at`, a `reason`, and for each file its generator, path, SHA-256, and the shot ids
it covers.
[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4b. Append the round to run.json] shasum -a 256 output/prompts/round-1/*.txt

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4b. Append the round to run.json] This is the only writeable part of `run.json`. Everything else was fixed when the
architect wrote it.

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 5. Hand off] Tell the user where the files are. Offer the next step:
"Want me to QA the generated images against the storyboard? Use `visual-asset-critic` once you have the renders."

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 5. Hand off] For paste-into-generator workflows, the user can pipe individual shots to the clipboard with the bundled helper:
python tools/copy-prompt.py output/prompts/round-1/midjourney.txt
python tools/copy-prompt.py output/prompts/round-2/revised-midjourney.txt --shot shot_03

[Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 5. Hand off] This is optional. The `.txt` files are also directly readable, and the user can copy any block by hand. The helper exists for the case where the operator is bouncing between the terminal and a generator UI repeatedly.

[Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop)] This is what `visual-asset-critic`'s structured output is for. When the user hands you `shots.json` plus one or more `critique.json` files (the machine-readable verdict the critic writes), don't re-forge the whole storyboard, re-emit prompts for **only the shots that failed**, with the fix already applied.

[Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Trigger] The user says "apply the critique", "revise the failed shots", "re-roll what didn't pass", or hands over an output tree containing `critiques/`.

[Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow] 1. Read every critique under `output/critiques/round-{N}/`, where N is the highest round
   present. Each file is one shot's verdict (`shot_id`, `verdict`, `issues[]`).
[Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow] 2. Skip any with `verdict: ACCEPT`. Those are done.
